chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Hanzala, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I married a woman, so I asked around about her, and it was said (certain things) about her.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'And you, why did you ask around about her as well? The investigation is not upon you.'
ai.seo_question: Is a husband required to investigate his wife's background before marriage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Umar ibn Hanzala seeks the Imam’s ruling on pre-marital inquiry, to which Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while asking is permissible, the husband is not obligated to conduct exhaustive investigation (*taftish*). This establishes the principle of *istishab* (presumption of innocence/validity) in marital relations, distinguishing between voluntary due diligence and mandatory scrutiny. The ruling underscores the Shia legal emphasis on ease and the avoidance of unnecessary hardship in family law.
